headline: Strawberry Rhubarb Streusel Muffins Recipe
description: These tender, vanilla-scented muffins are full of strawberry and rhubarb, making them perfect for spring.
name: Strawberry Rhubarb Streusel Muffins Recipe
keywords: breakfast sweets, rhubarb, wake and bake
recipeIngredient: 16 tablespoons (2 sticks) unsalted butter, melted and cooled

recipeInstructions.text: For the Muffins: Adjust oven rack to center position and preheat oven to 375°F (190°C). Butter muffin tins or line with paper holders. In a small bowl, combine rhubarb and sugar. Let stand 20 minutes.

In a large bowl, whisk together flour, brown sugar, baking powder, and salt. In a medium bowl, whisk together milk, eggs, butter, and vanilla until combined. Pour wet ingredients into dry ingredients and stir until combined (lumps will remain.) Use a plastic spatula or wooden spoon to gently fold in rhubarb, sugar, and strawberries until combined.
For the Topping : In a medium bowl, combine butter, sugar, and flour. Rub butter into flour until crumbs form.

Fill each muffin cup 3/4 full with batter. Top with streusel. Bake muffins until golden and a cake tester comes out clean, about 20 minutes. Let cool in tin for 5 minutes. Repeat with remaining batches of muffins. Store muffins in a sealed container at room temperature for up to 3 days.

review.reviewBody: I wanted to love this recipe but there must be a mistake in it - the muffins are waaayyyy too buttery. After baking them, butter literally oozed out of the muffins and they were way too soft. (I left the juices in after letting the rhubarb sit in the sugar.) Then I left them covered in a sealed container and that was a big mistake - they got even softer. After 2 days of sitting uncovered and a period left in a warm but not hot oven to dry them out they were edible. Also, the streusel is not the best - again too buttery and not enough oomph. PS - Mine looked nothing like the photo. they caved in and did not have that nice outside crumb.

It's about four years since this was posted, but I have a question. The recipe calls for 1 1/2 cups milk but doesn't specify what kind (2%, whole, etc.?) Will 2% or nonfat work, as that is what I have in the house.
after the rhubarb sits for 20 minutes, it will release some juice - should the juice that comes out be discarded or folded into the batter with strawberries and rhubarb in step 2?
